scope: Fresh generation of an already-developed concept through the canonical restricted runtime, no target seed; not held-out quality

meaning.evidence: Inside the coin ring a Y-shaped glyph descends from ~y=4 to a junction at centre (native row 7, x6-x9 = 20) with a short stem below, crossed by two full-width horizontal bars at rows 8 and 10. Two crossbars over a Y is yen; the reference won glyph is a doubled W and the lira/ruble references show a single stem with ascender or bowl.
meaning.treatment: No defect observed; no treatment needed.

style.evidence: Ring weight ~2px at 16px (row 8, x1-x2 = 97/73) matches the reference coin rings, crossbars use flat butt terminals, and the glyph is inset from the ring with a clear ~2px margin (row 8, x3-x4 = 255) as in the reference lira/ruble/won glyphs. Outlined and filled paints are delivered in the same pairing as the reference family.
style.treatment: No defect observed; no treatment needed.

optics.evidence: At 16px 1x both crossbars are solid (rows 8 and 10: outlined x5-x10 = 32,0,0,0,0,32; filled x21-x26 = 218,255,255,255,255,218) and the gap between them stays fully open (row 9 outlined x5-x6 and x9-x10 = 255; filled row 9 x19-x22 = 0), with the Y arms distinct across rows 4-7 on white and black. The vertical stem is the lightest element (127 between the bars, 166/87 below the lower bar) but is rendered, not collapsed, and is crisp at 2x.
optics.treatment: No collapsed feature observed; if extra safety were wanted the stem below the lower bar could be nudged toward the pixel grid, but nothing here requires it.

family.evidence: Coin diameter is identical across paints (outlined x1-x14, filled x17-x30, both 14px), and the crossbars sit on rows 8 and 10 with the arm junction on row 7 in both halves of native.png. Differences are limited to paint inversion and knockout weighting of the glyph.
family.treatment: No defect observed; no treatment needed.

unresolved.description: At 16px the 1.5-unit detail stem centered at x=12 maps to a native pixel boundary, so its isolated segment is split across two antialiased columns and has lower peak contrast than the half-pixel-aligned horizontal bars. The stem remains readable in both paints; shifting it to a full-contrast column would visibly decenter the yen glyph.

meaning.evidence: The enlarged vectors show two diagonals converging into a short vertical stem, crossed by two full-width horizontal bars, inside a coin ring. That Y-plus-two-bars form is ¥, not the doubled W arms of the won reference nor an S or C-with-bars.
meaning.treatment: None needed; the glyph reads as yen.

style.evidence: Against references.png (lira, peso, won coins), the candidate matches outer ring diameter, ring stroke weight, and the disc-with-knockout filled treatment; its glyph strokes carry the same apparent weight and share of the counter, and its flat-ended crossbars match the peso's flat-ended bars.
style.treatment: None needed; no reference mismatch observed.

optics.evidence: At 16px the bars stay separated: outlined row y=9 is 255 across x=3-12 except the 127 stem, filled row y=9 is 0 except 127/127 at x=23-24, and the V arms hold (20-122 outlined, 137-207 filled) on both surfaces. The only weakness is the stem descender below the lower bar, a single half-coverage row (132 outlined y=11, 122 filled) that is gone by y=12 (246 / 8).
optics.treatment: Extend the vertical stem by about 0.5 unit, or raise the lower crossbar slightly, so the descender lands on a full pixel row at 16px 1x.

family.evidence: Both paints place the crossbars on the same rows (y=8 and y=10) at the same 6px width (x=5-10 outlined, x=21-26 filled) with identical coin extents (rows 1-14). Differences are limited to the deliberate ring-vs-solid-disc and polarity change.
family.treatment: None needed; concept, scale and layout are consistent across paints.

unresolved.description: At 16px the 1.5-unit detail stem centered at x=12 maps to a native pixel boundary, so its isolated between-bar segment is split evenly across two antialiased columns (127/127) and has lower peak contrast than the half-pixel-aligned horizontal bars. Extending the lower endpoint to y=17.5 improves terminal survival in both paints, but shifting the stem to a full-contrast native column would visibly decenter the yen glyph.

billing: Native subscriptions; list-price review estimates are not API bills
observation: Both reviewers pass meaning/style/optics/family. Both authors retain the centered-stem antialiasing limitation. Attempt2 extends the stem endpoint by0.5 canonical units but retains the same limitation and does not improve a failing reviewer dimension, so the loop preserves attempt1. The first reviewer incorrectly calls visibly round terminals flat butt terminals. Deliberate optical tradeoff versus actionable author defect remains unresolved; do not relabel this run approved.
